title: Herod kills James; Peter's angelic prison release + the death of Herod

paragraphs.text: Now about that time Herod the king put forth his hands to afflict certain of the church.
paragraphs.original: Κατʼ ἐκεῖνον δὲ τὸν καιρὸν ἐπέβαλεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ βασιλεὺς τὰς χεῖρας κακῶσαί τινας τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
paragraphs.translit: Katʼ ekeinon de ton kairon epebalen Hērōdēs ho basileus tas cheiras kakōsai tinas tōn apo tēs ekklēsias.

paragraphs.text: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
paragraphs.original: ἀνεῖλεν δὲ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰωάννου μαχαίρῃ.
paragraphs.translit: aneilen de Iakōbon ton adelphon Iōannou machairē.

paragraphs.text: And when he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. And [those] were the days of unleavened bread.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὅτι ἀρεστόν ἐστιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον (ἦσαν δὲ ἡμέραι τῶν ἀζύμων),
paragraphs.translit: idōn de hoti areston estin tois Ioudaiois prosetheto syllabein kai Petron (ēsan de hēmerai tōn azymōn),

paragraphs.text: And when he had taken him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to guard him; intending after the Passover to bring him forth to the people.
paragraphs.original: ὃν καὶ πιάσας ἔθετο εἰς φυλακήν, παραδοὺς τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις στρατιωτῶν φυλάσσειν αὐτόν, βουλόμενος μετὰ τὸ πάσχα ἀναγαγεῖν αὐτὸν τῷ λαῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hon kai piasas etheto eis phylakēn, paradous tessarsin tetradiois stratiōtōn phylassein auton, boulomenos meta to pascha anagagein auton tō laō.

paragraphs.text: Peter therefore was kept in the prison: but prayer was made earnestly of the church unto God for him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν Πέτρος ἐτηρεῖτο ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· προσευχὴ δὲ ἦν ἐκτενῶς γινομένη ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὸν θεὸν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho men oun Petros etēreito en tē phylakē· proseuchē de ēn ektenōs ginomenē hypo tēs ekklēsias pros ton theon peri autou.

paragraphs.text: And when Herod was about to bring him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and guards before the door kept the prison.
paragraphs.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἤμελλεν προαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἡρῴδης, τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ ἦν ὁ Πέτρος κοιμώμενος μεταξὺ δύο στρατιωτῶν δεδεμένος ἁλύσεσιν δυσίν, φύλακές τε πρὸ τῆς θύρας ἐτήρουν τὴν φυλακήν.
paragraphs.translit: Hote de ēmellen proagagein auton ho Hērōdēs, tē nykti ekeinē ēn ho Petros koimōmenos metaxy dyo stratiōtōn dedemenos halysesin dysin, phylakes te pro tēs thyras etēroun tēn phylakēn.

paragraphs.text: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shined in the cell: and he smote Peter on the side, and awoke him, saying, Rise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπέστη, καὶ φῶς ἔλαμψεν ἐν τῷ οἰκήματι· πατάξας δὲ τὴν πλευρὰν τοῦ Πέτρου ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστα ἐν τάχει· καὶ ἐξέπεσαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἁλύσεις ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou angelos kyriou epestē, kai phōs elampsen en tō oikēmati· pataxas de tēn pleuran tou Petrou ēgeiren auton legōn· Anasta en tachei· kai exepesan autou hai halyseis ek tōn cheirōn.

paragraphs.text: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And he did so. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ζῶσαι καὶ ὑπόδησαι τὰ σανδάλιά σου· ἐποίησεν δὲ οὕτως. καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Περιβαλοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου καὶ ἀκολούθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho angelos pros auton· Zōsai kai hypodēsai ta sandalia sou· epoiēsen de houtōs. kai legei autō· Peribalou to himation sou kai akolouthei moi.

paragraphs.text: And he went out, and followed; and he knew not that it was true which was done by the angel, but thought he saw a vision.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἠκολούθει, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τὸ γινόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, ἐδόκει δὲ ὅραμα βλέπειν.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthōn ēkolouthei, kai ouk ēdei hoti alēthes estin to ginomenon dia tou angelou, edokei de horama blepein.

paragraphs.text: And when they were past the first and the second guard, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth into the city; which opened to them of its own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and straightway the angel departed from him.
paragraphs.original: διελθόντες δὲ πρώτην φυλακὴν καὶ δευτέραν ἦλθαν ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην τὴν σιδηρᾶν τὴν φέρουσαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἥτις αὐτομάτη ἠνοίγη αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐξελθόντες προῆλθον ῥύμην μίαν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέστη ὁ ἄγγελος ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: dielthontes de prōtēn phylakēn kai deuteran ēlthan epi tēn pylēn tēn sidēran tēn pherousan eis tēn polin, hētis automatē ēnoigē autois, kai exelthontes proēlthon rhymēn mian, kai eutheōs apestē ho angelos apʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a truth, that the Lord hath sent forth his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος εἶπεν· Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ κύριος τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατό με ἐκ χειρὸς Ἡρῴδου καὶ πάσης τῆς προσδοκίας τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Petros en heautō genomenos eipen· Nyn oida alēthōs hoti exapesteilen ho kyrios ton angelon autou kai exeilato me ek cheiros Hērōdou kai pasēs tēs prosdokias tou laou tōn Ioudaiōn.

paragraphs.text: And when he had considered [the thing], he came to the house of Mary the mother of John whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together and were praying.
paragraphs.original: Συνιδών τε ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν τῆς Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐπικαλουμένου Μάρκου, οὗ ἦσαν ἱκανοὶ συνηθροισμένοι καὶ προσευχόμενοι.
paragraphs.translit: Synidōn te ēlthen epi tēn oikian tēs Marias tēs mētros Iōannou tou epikaloumenou Markou, hou ēsan hikanoi synēthroismenoi kai proseuchomenoi.

paragraphs.text: And when he knocked at the door of the gate, a maid came to answer, named Rhoda.
paragraphs.original: κρούσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν θύραν τοῦ πυλῶνος προσῆλθε παιδίσκη ὑπακοῦσαι ὀνόματι Ῥόδη,
paragraphs.translit: krousantos de autou tēn thyran tou pylōnos prosēlthe paidiskē hypakousai onomati Rhodē,

paragraphs.text: And when she knew Peter`s voice, she opened not the gate for joy, but ran in, and told that Peter stood before the gate.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ Πέτρου ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἤνοιξεν τὸν πυλῶνα, εἰσδραμοῦσα δὲ ἀπήγγειλεν ἑστάναι τὸν Πέτρον πρὸ τοῦ πυλῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: kai epignousa tēn phōnēn tou Petrou apo tēs charas ouk ēnoixen ton pylōna, eisdramousa de apēngeilen hestanai ton Petron pro tou pylōnos.

paragraphs.text: And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she confidently affirmed that it was even so. And they said, It is his angel.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπαν· Μαίνῃ. ἡ δὲ διϊσχυρίζετο οὕτως ἔχειν. οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον· Ὁ ἄγγελός ἐστιν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de pros autēn eipan· Mainē. hē de diischyrizeto houtōs echein. hoi de elegon· Ho angelos estin autou.

paragraphs.text: But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐπέμενεν κρούων· ἀνοίξαντες δὲ εἶδαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξέστησαν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Petros epemenen krouōn· anoixantes de eidan auton kai exestēsan.

paragraphs.text: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him forth out of the prison. And he said, Tell these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went to another place.
paragraphs.original: κατασείσας δὲ αὐτοῖς τῇ χειρὶ σιγᾶν διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ὁ κύριος αὐτὸν ἐξήγαγεν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς, εἶπέν τε· Ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰακώβῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ταῦτα. καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἕτερον τόπον.
paragraphs.translit: kataseisas de autois tē cheiri sigan diēgēsato autois pōs ho kyrios auton exēgagen ek tēs phylakēs, eipen te· Apangeilate Iakōbō kai tois adelphois tauta. kai exelthōn eporeuthē eis heteron topon.

paragraphs.text: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.
paragraphs.original: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἦν τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις, τί ἄρα ὁ Πέτρος ἐγένετο.
paragraphs.translit: Genomenēs de hēmeras ēn tarachos ouk oligos en tois stratiōtais, ti ara ho Petros egeneto.

paragraphs.text: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the guards, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judaea to Caesarea, and tarried there.
paragraphs.original: Ἡρῴδης δὲ ἐπιζητήσας αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ εὑρὼν ἀνακρίνας τοὺς φύλακας ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι, καὶ κατελθὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς Καισάρειαν διέτριβεν.
paragraphs.translit: Hērōdēs de epizētēsas auton kai mē heurōn anakrinas tous phylakas ekeleusen apachthēnai, kai katelthōn apo tēs Ioudaias eis Kaisareian dietriben.

paragraphs.text: Now he was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: and they came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus the king`s chamberlain their friend, they asked for peace, because their country was fed from the king`s country.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ θυμομαχῶν Τυρίοις καὶ Σιδωνίοις· ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ παρῆσαν πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ πείσαντες Βλάστον τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος τοῦ βασιλέως ᾐτοῦντο εἰρήνην διὰ τὸ τρέφεσθαι αὐτῶν τὴν χώραν ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλικῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de thymomachōn Tyriois kai Sidōniois· homothymadon de parēsan pros auton, kai peisantes Blaston ton epi tou koitōnos tou basileōs ētounto eirēnēn dia to trephesthai autōn tēn chōran apo tēs basilikēs.

paragraphs.text: And upon a set day Herod arrayed himself in royal apparel, and sat on the throne, and made an oration unto them.
paragraphs.original: τακτῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐνδυσάμενος ἐσθῆτα βασιλικὴν καὶ καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐδημηγόρει πρὸς αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: taktē de hēmera ho Hērōdēs endysamenos esthēta basilikēn kai kathisas epi tou bēmatos edēmēgorei pros autous·

paragraphs.text: And the people shouted, [saying], The voice of a god, and not of a man.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ δῆμος ἐπεφώνει· Θεοῦ φωνὴ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de dēmos epephōnei· Theou phōnē kai ouk anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: And immediately an angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.
paragraphs.original: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐπάταξεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος κυρίου ἀνθʼ ὧν οὐκ ἔδωκεν τὴν δόξαν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ γενόμενος σκωληκόβρωτος ἐξέψυξεν.
paragraphs.translit: parachrēma de epataxen auton angelos kyriou anthʼ hōn ouk edōken tēn doxan tō theō, kai genomenos skōlēkobrōtos exepsyxen.

paragraphs.text: But the word of God grew and multiplied.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο.
paragraphs.translit: Ho de logos tou theou ēuxanen kai eplēthyneto.

paragraphs.text: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministration, taking with them John whose surname was Mark.
paragraphs.original: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν, εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν, συμπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάννην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μᾶρκον.
paragraphs.translit: Barnabas de kai Saulos hypestrepsan, eis Ierousalēm plērōsantes tēn diakonian, symparalabontes Iōannēn ton epiklēthenta Markon.
